_notes.purpose: The static capability table (ADPT-02, TECHNICAL-DESIGN 5.6). It is read by the server, because it holds protocol and agent facts that must hold for users of the server without the app (ADPT-03); the app receives the already resolved row in hello and adapts only its UI.
_notes.rows: One row per agent id, in the committed adapter order of ADPT-06 (Claude Code, then Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode), with the unknown row last. Rows with status planned exist so that an adapter enters the table in that order rather than appearing out of nowhere when it ships.
_notes.null: null means the field has not been measured for that agent yet. The server treats it as the value of the unknown row for the same field (5.6), so a planned row already behaves like a base-support client. It never means false.
_notes.match: HANDOFF_AGENT is compared against match.env, and clientInfo.name of the MCP handshake against match.client_names. The values agents send are not documented (A-08) and are recorded per version by the canary suite (test/canary, docs/agent-facts.md), which is the only thing that may fill these lists. claude-code sends clientInfo.name = claude-code, measured on 2026-09-08 against Claude Code 2.1.263; codex sends codex-mcp-client, measured on 2026-09-10 against Codex 0.153.4; opencode sends opencode, measured on 2026-09-11 against OpenCode 1.18.29; Cursor's editor sends cursor-vscode and its CLI sends Cursor, both measured on 2026-09-11 against Cursor 3.20.10 and the CLI 2026.09.10-fd3934a; VS Code sends Visual Studio Code and the GitHub Copilot CLI sends copilot-cli, both measured on 2026-09-11 against VS Code 1.137.0 and the CLI 1.0.83. VS Code's name is its own rather than Copilot's: it is the MCP client of VS Code's chat, which is GitHub Copilot's. The unknown row matches nothing and is the fallback.
_notes.tool_timeout_ms_default: The timeout the agent applies to a tool call when its entry configures none, in milliseconds. It stays null for Claude Code, for Codex and for GitHub Copilot: the canary can only bound their default from below (a call with nothing configured ran 70 s uncut in Claude Code, 120 s in Codex, 90 s in the Copilot CLI, docs/agent-facts.md, and VS Code's MCP client sends a tool call with no timeout of its own), and a number that is a lower bound rather than the value would make the heartbeat arithmetic of 5.6 lie. null already produces the safe answer, the 50 s heartbeat of the unknown row. OpenCode's is a value: it passes the entry's timeout to the MCP SDK, whose own default is 60 000 ms, and a call with nothing configured was cut at 59 944 ms (measured on 2026-09-11). Cursor's is the one of its CLI, which hands a tool call to the MCP SDK with no timeout of its own, so the SDK's 60 000 ms applies (measured on 2026-09-11); the editor's own limit is longer, a 120 000 ms idle timeout that restarts on progress (read from the 3.20.10 bundle), and the shorter of the two surfaces is the one a heartbeat has to beat. The heartbeat both yield is the 50 s floor. The installer normally writes HANDOFF_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS anyway, which outranks this field; nothing derives from it except the heartbeat. For Cursor it must not: Cursor has no per-server timeout to raise, so a larger HANDOFF_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS would move the heartbeat past the cut.
_notes.heartbeat_after_ms: The heartbeat used when no timeout can be resolved at all. Only the unknown row carries it (UNKNOWN_CLIENT_HEARTBEAT_MS = 50000, TOOL-06a); every other row inherits it through the null rule until its own timeout is known.
_notes.per_server_timeout_field: The name of the per-server timeout field of that agent's MCP entry, written by the installer when the agent has one (A-04). Informational for the server: the timeout it uses comes from the environment or from tool_timeout_ms_default. The unit is the agent's: Claude Code's timeout is in milliseconds, Codex's tool_timeout_sec in seconds (20 cut a call at 20 s, measured on 2026-09-10), OpenCode's timeout in milliseconds again (20000 cut a call at 20 003 ms, measured on 2026-09-11), so an installer writing 1800000 ms for Claude Code writes 1800 for Codex and 1800000 for OpenCode. Cursor has none: neither its editor nor its CLI reads a timeout from an MCP entry (3.20.10), so the field is null. GitHub Copilot's is the CLI's timeout of an mcp-config.json entry, in milliseconds (20000 cut a call at 20 010 ms, measured on 2026-09-11 against the CLI 1.0.83); VS Code's mcp.json has no such field, so the field is the CLI's alone.
_notes.session_identity: How the app keys a session: parent_pid for a CLI agent, ancestor_chain:editor where the process parent is the editor and the chain must be matched at the editor level (ADPT-02, R-12). The row says what the agent's editor surface needs. Each session resolves its own (src/adapters/editor.ts, T-069), because one agent can arrive with or without an editor above it — Cursor's CLI shares the cursor row and is parent_pid, and so does the GitHub Copilot CLI share the copilot row with VS Code — and hello carries ancestor_chain:editor only for a session whose chain shows the editor starting the server.
_notes.unknown_match: TECHNICAL-DESIGN 5.6 prints the unknown row's match as {}; it is written here with both fields explicit (env null, no client names) so that every row has the same shape and the schema can close it.
